segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: I haven’t seen you for a bit, Marie.

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: No. I’ve been busy with my project.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: You’re making a vegan alternative to eggs, aren’t you? Something that doesn’t use animal products?

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: Yes. I’m using chickpeas. I had two main aims when I first started looking for an alternative to eggs, but actually I’ve found chickpeas have got more advantages.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Right.

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: But how about your project on reusing waste food – you were looking at bread, weren’t you?

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Yes. It’s been hard work, but I’ve enjoyed it. The basic process was quite straightforward – breaking the stale bread down to a paste then reforming it.

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: But you were using 3-D printing, weren’t you, to make the paste into biscuits?

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Yeah, I’d used that before, but in this project, I had time to play around with different patterns for the biscuits and finding how I could add fruit and vegetables to make them a more appetising colour, and I was really pleased with what I managed to produce. _Q21/22_

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: It must’ve been a great feeling to make something appetising out of bits of old bread that would’ve been thrown away otherwise. _Q21/22_

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: It was. And I’m hoping that some of the restaurants in town will be interested in the biscuits. I’m going to send them some samples.

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: I came across something on the internet yesterday that might interest you. It was a company that’s developed touch-sensitive sensors for food labels.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Mmm?

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: It’s a special sort of label on the food package. When the label’s smooth, the food is fresh and then when you can feel bumps on the label, that means the food’s gone bad. It started off as a project to help visually impaired people know whether food was fit to eat or not.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Interesting. So just solid food?

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: No, things like milk and juice as well. But actually, I thought it might be really good for drug storage in hospitals and pharmacies. _Q23/24_

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Right. And coming back to food, maybe it’d be possible to use it for other things besides freshness. Like how many kilograms a joint of meat is. for example. _Q23/24_

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: Yes, there’s all sorts of possibilities.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: I was reading an article about food trends predicting how eating habits might change in the next few years.

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: Oh – things like more focus on local products? That seems so obvious, but the shops are still full of imported foods.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Yes, they need to be more proactive to address that.

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: And somehow motivate consumers to change, yes.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: One thing everyone’s aware of is the need for a reduction in unnecessary packaging – but just about everything you buy in supermarkets is still covered in plastic. The government needs to do something about it.

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: Absolutely. It’s got to change.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Do you think there’ll be more interest in gluten – and lactose-free food?

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: For people with allergies or food intolerances? I don’t know. Lots of people I know have been buying that type of food for years now.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Yes, even if they haven’t been diagnosed with an allergy.

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: That’s right. One thing I ’ve noticed is the number of branded products related to celebrity chefs – people watch them cooking on TV and then buy things like spice mixes or frozen foods with the chef’s name on . . . I bought something like that once, but I won’t again.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Yeah – I bought a ready-made spice mix for chicken which was supposed to be used by a chef I’d seen on television, and it didn’t actually taste of anything.

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: Mm. Did the article mention ‘ghost kitchens’ used to produce takeaway food?

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: No. What are they?

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: Well, they might have the name of a restaurant, but actually they’re a cooking facility just for delivery meals – the public don’t ever go there. But people aren’t aware of that – it’s all kept very quiet.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: So people don’t realise the food’s not actually from the restaurant?

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: Right.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Did you know more and more people are using all sorts of different mushrooms now, to treat different health concerns? Things like heart problems?

segments.speaker: MARIE
segments.en: Hmm. They might be taking a big risk there.

segments.speaker: COLIN
segments.en: Yes, it’s hard to know which varieties are safe to eat. Anyway maybe now...
